why: The light-roast pole of Brooklyn: rotating single origins, a big quiet room with high ceilings, pour-over is the point. Closest match to your anaerobic / co-ferment taste; ask what's on that isn't on the menu.
Colombian direct-trade, roasted on site, skylit room full of plants. Roast sits a touch darker than Sey; the space is the draw for a long read.
The 2005 original beside its own roastery. Pour-over is still the best thing here; unfussy, plenty of seats, 7–6 daily.

a: 368 Grand St, Williamsburg · 142 Driggs Ave, Greenpoint
why: The reliable one: solid roast program, tables, outlets, Driggs is open until 9. Not a tasting destination; the place you go when you want to be sure you'll get a seat.
Aussie-style roastery with a proper pour-over bar. Beautiful room, but crowded by 10 on weekends — go on your Tuesday.
Family-run Colombian roaster, roasts on site, Colombian pastries. Small and early — weekdays 6:30–3 — so it's a Friday-morning place, not an afternoon one.
Flowers and coffee in one room; calm, good light, the kind of place a book actually gets read. Coffee is good rather than serious.
The nearest real roaster to the apartment. Norwegian-leaning, small, no fuss. Your default when the morning is short.
Tasting flights and experimental processes are their whole thing — the most anaerobic-forward program in the city. Badminton mornings put you ten minutes away.
Aarhus light-roast Nordic style, the closest thing here to the Tokyo omakase shops. Bakery is half the reason people go.
Greenpoint roaster with a real pour-over bar on Freeman. Worth one Friday when you want a longer walk.
Small Brooklyn team roasting light-to-medium in a New York–Nordic style; keeps coming up next to Sey in current guides. Do both in one Bushwick morning.
New Greenpoint bar pouring Sey on espresso plus guest pour-overs from other roasters — a multi-roaster program a few blocks from home.
Their training lab runs pour-over classes and cuppings. One cupping during the sabbatical fits the competition-barista curiosity without becoming a project.
